# Start here

Every agent doc for this repo lives in `.agents/`. The root `AGENTS.md` and
`CLAUDE.md` only point here. This file is the operating contract for **any**
agent or engineer: concrete commands, explicit rules, no tribal knowledge. When
the way we work changes, change it here.

## What this repo is

A reference scaffold for **agentic engineering**: the files, gates, and context
that make AI-written code consistent and enterprise-grade. TypeScript + React is
just the runnable carrier. The scaffolding is the point (see the root
`README.md` and [`NORTH_STAR.md`](NORTH_STAR.md)).

## Run it

```bash
pnpm install          # install dependencies (Node ≥ 22.18, pnpm)
pnpm setup:agents     # install the external agentic toolkit (one time)
pnpm dev              # run web (http://localhost:5173) and api (:3001) together; Vite proxies /trpc
pnpm lint:policy      # ESLint: policy, React hooks, and React Compiler rules
pnpm arch:check       # architecture gate, structure check, diagram freshness, API report freshness
pnpm arch:diagram     # regenerate docs/architecture/roles.mmd and each result's architecture.mmd
pnpm api:report       # regenerate each package's etc/*.api.md after an intended export change
pnpm verify           # the full local gate suite (typecheck → biome → eslint → react doctor → fallow → architecture → tests → build)
pnpm e2e              # playwright test: every spec in each result's web/e2e/, with its api and web servers
```

## Run a Todo trial

The orchestrator runs each Todo trial; an agent inside a trial builds its
result from the prompt alone. Run trials one at a time, from the checkout
that keeps the evidence, at the scaffold revision every trial shares
([ADR 0034](decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)):

```bash
pnpm trial --trial 1 --scaffold <rev> --trials-root <dir> --dry-run   # print the plan and the exact claude argv
pnpm trial --trial 1 --scaffold <rev> --trials-root <dir>             # clone, run one fresh session, check, record
git fetch <dir>/todo-01-<stamp>/repo trial/todo-01:trial/todo-01         # keep the result branch
```

Pass `--agent codex` for a fresh Codex exec session (default: `claude`).
Pass `--task /absolute/path/task.json` for a task file; a task with a target
repository pins its own revision and needs no `--scaffold`. Task-local prompts
and acceptance commands stay outside the clone. External tasks use `land: patch`
and can set an absolute `evidenceDir` to keep private evidence outside this repo.
See [ADR 0048](decisions/0048-trial-tasks-and-codex.md). Todo Codex ids are
`todo-codex-01..03`; compare keeps Todo runs and proves baselines per agent.

The run writes `docs/trials/todo-01.json`, the agent's stream as
`todo-01.stream.jsonl` with secrets redacted (and `todo-01.patch` when it
fails), and prints its workdir. Fetch the result branch, then remove the
workdir before the next trial; the harness refuses to start while one
remains. Pass `--retry` only after a failure from before the agent started.

Each trial's commands use a private temp and cache folder inside its
workdir, and bubblewrap (`bwrap`) mounts that temp folder over `/tmp`, so the
agent sees only its own `/tmp` files. Install bubblewrap first: a trial fails
before its agent starts when `bwrap` fails to run. No time limit
applies. Stop a trial with Ctrl-C, and read how long it took from
`run.durationMs` and `run.agentDurationMs` in its record
([ADR 0038](decisions/0038-trial-isolation-and-no-time-limit.md)).

After the three trials, merge each passed result branch with `git merge --no-ff`,
commit every record, stream and patch, and run
`node tooling/trial/compare.mjs` to write `docs/trials/comparison.md`: the
full pass count, the shared baseline and each difference between the runs,
classified against the spec freedoms of
[ADR 0035](decisions/0035-trial-comparison.md) and
[ADR 0037](decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md).

## The golden rules

1. **Read before you write.** Architecture, conventions, the Definition of Done,
   the glossary, and ADRs live in this folder.
2. **Follow the patterns; copy the templates.** New files come from
   [`templates/`](templates/). Consistency is the deliverable.
3. **Behaviour is defined by the E2E map**, each result's `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`
   (for example `apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`), not by the implementation.
   Add behaviour there first. A feature's PRD in `docs/prd/` states its intent
   and links each behaviour to the test that proves it.
4. **When a gate fails, fix the cause.** Keep every gate and its config as it
   is; the checks below enforce this.
5. **Done means the gates are green.** Report a task complete once
   `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass; see
   [`project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md`](project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md).
6. **PRs carry proof.** Complete the pull request template and follow
   [`project/PR_QUALITY.md`](project/PR_QUALITY.md) before opening a PR or
   marking it ready.
7. **Change rules in the open.** When a constraint is wrong, propose an ADR in
   [`decisions/`](decisions/) and change the rule there.

## Rules and what enforces them

Each rule below fails a check when it is broken, so the check's message is the
first place to look. [`project/CONVENTIONS.md`](project/CONVENTIONS.md) lists
the code-level rules and their checks.

| Rule | Enforced by |
| --- | --- |
| Every file has one architecture role, and imports follow the role table and the contract in [`project/ARCHITECTURE.md`](project/ARCHITECTURE.md). | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate`, `pnpm fallow:audit`, `pnpm typecheck` |
| Commits, PR titles, and branch names follow Conventional Commits. | commitlint on `commit-msg`; `PR quality` workflow |
| Every hook runs; `--no-verify`, `git commit -n`, `HUSKY=0`, and `core.hooksPath`, alias, or config-include overrides are refused. | `.claude/hooks/block-gate-bypass.sh` (Claude Code and trusted Codex sessions with hook trust, [ADR 0027](decisions/0027-block-common-hook-bypasses.md)); CI re-runs every gate |
| A change that loosens or rewrites a gate (`.husky/**`, `.github/workflows/**`, `eslint.config.js`, `biome.json`, `commitlint.config.ts`, `tooling/eslint-plugin-policy.js`, `scripts/check-suppressions.mjs`, `scripts/enforcement-approval.mjs`, `scripts/enforcement-approval.test.ts`) waits for BenSheridanEdwards to tick the sign-off for its head commit. A tick counts when it is made as BenSheridanEdwards. | `enforcement-approval` status ([ADR 0023](decisions/0023-protect-only-the-files-that-run-the-gates.md), [ADR 0024](decisions/0024-sign-off-only-loosening-enforcement-changes.md)) |
| Done means every gate is green on the latest commit. | `Required gates` and the checks in `docs/required-gates.md` |
| A PR body keeps the template sections and carries inline proof. | `PR quality` workflow (`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`) |
| A new dependency arrives with an ADR. | `pnpm check:adr` |
| Secrets stay out of commits. | gitleaks in pre-commit and CI |
| An ESLint exception lives in `eslint.config.js` with its reason; an inline `eslint-disable*`, `/* eslint <rule>: off */` or `/* global */` comment fails lint in every source file. | `pnpm lint:policy` (`noInlineConfig`, [ADR 0039](decisions/0039-block-inline-lint-disable-comments.md)) |
| Every type suppression is a `@ts-expect-error` with its reason, and every `biome-ignore` carries its reason. | `pnpm check:suppressions`; Biome for `biome-ignore` |
| Generated files match their source. | `pnpm arch:check`, `pnpm gates:check`, `pnpm api:check` |
| Gate and tooling scripts match a glob with `matchesGlob` from `node:path` or the tool's own file list. | `pnpm lint:policy` ([ADR 0041](decisions/0041-scripts-ask-the-tool-which-files-a-glob-covers.md)) |
| A test's child process starts from the allowlisted environment in `scripts/jest-global-setup.mjs`; a test passes any other variable it needs in `env`. | Jest `globalSetup` and `scripts/jest-env.test.ts` ([ADR 0042](decisions/0042-test-child-processes-get-an-allowlisted-environment.md)) |
| Guidance docs state rules as the action to take. | `pnpm check:docs` |
| Each PRD in `docs/prd/` links every behaviour it lists to the E2E test that proves it. | `pnpm check:docs` ([ADR 0045](decisions/0045-prds-state-intent-and-link-their-specs.md)) |
| A doc that ties sign-off to a file names only a file the enforcement gate guards. | `pnpm check:docs` ([ADR 0030](decisions/0030-docs-name-only-guarded-paths-for-sign-off.md)) |

## Simplicity Mode

Use Ponytail for coding, review, refactor, and design tasks unless the user says
otherwise. Default level: `full`: delete code, reuse existing patterns, and use
stdlib or native platform features before adding abstractions or dependencies.

## What is here, and when to read it

| Path | Read it when… |
| --- | --- |
| [`project/AGENTIC_INFRASTRUCTURE.md`](project/AGENTIC_INFRASTRUCTURE.md) | …before changing agent guidance, hooks, workflows, or skills. |
| [`project/ARCHITECTURE.md`](project/ARCHITECTURE.md) | …before adding or moving any module: the role table, the api file roles, the state model, and how to add a route, a feature or a procedure. It is the pattern you must follow. |
| [`project/CONVENTIONS.md`](project/CONVENTIONS.md) | …while writing code: naming, structure, imports, errors, state. |
| [`project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md`](project/DEFINITION_OF_DONE.md) | …before you claim a task is finished. The gates enforce this list. |
| [`project/QUALITY_GATES.md`](project/QUALITY_GATES.md) | …before changing hooks, scripts, CI, or tool ownership. |
| [`project/PR_QUALITY.md`](project/PR_QUALITY.md) | …before opening, updating, or marking a pull request ready. |
| [`project/TECH_STACK.md`](project/TECH_STACK.md) | …to know which tool owns which concern (and what *not* to add). |
| [`project/GLOSSARY.md`](project/GLOSSARY.md) | …when you meet a domain term. Use these words exactly, in code and prose. |
| [`decisions/`](decisions/) | …to understand *why* a constraint exists before you challenge it. ADRs. |
| [`templates/`](templates/) | …when creating a new component, test, E2E flow, or PRD. Copy from here. |
| [`NORTH_STAR.md`](NORTH_STAR.md) | …to see where the repo is heading and why. |

| [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) | …to find handed-off work and its acceptance criteria. |
| [`CLAUDE_CODE.md`](CLAUDE_CODE.md) | …if you are Claude Code: skills, settings, hooks, and tooling. |
| [`GITNEXUS.md`](GITNEXUS.md) | …before editing a symbol: impact analysis and change detection. |
| [`openai.yaml`](openai.yaml) | …if you are an OpenAI-family agent: the same entry points as a manifest. |
| [`verify-agentic-template`](../.claude/skills/verify-agentic-template/SKILL.md) | …to drive the app and capture PR proof. |

## Safety

- Keep secrets out of commits; CI runs a secret scan and a dependency audit.
- Keep one owner per concern: Biome formats and runs general lint, ESLint runs
  policy and React rules, Jest and Playwright run tests. A new tool for an owned
  concern needs an ADR (see [`project/TECH_STACK.md`](project/TECH_STACK.md));
  `pnpm check:adr` fails a new dependency that no new ADR names.
- Treat generated artefacts (`apps/web/dist/`, `.cache/`, `coverage/`, `graphify-out/`,
  `.gitnexus/`) as disposable; regenerate them with their command.

# Architecture

> This is the anchor for **showcase #2**: agent-written code must follow the
> patterns described here. When asked to verify or review work, an agent checks
> the change against this document first.

## The shape

The repo is a pnpm workspace with one reference **result** and a UI kit
([ADR 0032](../decisions/0032-api-ui-greeting-and-contract.md)):

- A result is a pair of packages, `<root>/web` and `<root>/api`. The reference
  result lives in `apps/` (`@repo/web`, `@repo/api`). Each generated trial
  result lives in `showcase/<id>/` with the same shape.
- `packages/ui` (`@repo/ui`) holds the UI primitives every result renders with.
- `tooling/results.mjs` (`listResults`) is the one place that discovers
  results: the reference first, then each `showcase/<id>` that has both
  `web/package.json` and `api/package.json`, sorted by id.

The root configs own every gate and reach each package by glob, so a new result
joins every gate with no config entry of its own.

The reference implementation is the **greeting feature**: a name goes in, the
api greets it back. Copy its shape for every new feature.

```
apps/
├── web/                                 # @repo/web, Vite + React
│   ├── src/
│   │   ├── main.tsx                     # composition root: DOM, styles, ApiProvider
│   │   ├── App.tsx                      # mounts the routes; holds no business logic
│   │   ├── index.css
│   │   ├── api-client/                  # the only door to the api
│   │   │   ├── trpc.ts                  # useTrpc, TrpcProvider, RouterInputs, RouterOutputs
│   │   │   ├── ApiProvider.tsx          # real tRPC client over /trpc + QueryClient
│   │   │   ├── TestApiProvider.tsx      # the same providers over typed in-memory handlers
│   │   │   ├── testApiHandlers.ts       # TestApiHandlers, one handler per procedure path
│   │   │   ├── useTestApiClients.ts
│   │   │   └── index.ts                 # public surface
│   │   ├── routes/
│   │   │   └── greeting/                # one folder per route, kebab-case
│   │   │       ├── GreetingPage.tsx     # the page: composes the route's components
│   │   │       ├── GreetingForm.tsx     # one component per file
│   │   │       ├── GreetingMessage.tsx
│   │   │       ├── useGreeting.ts       # server state + local state
│   │   │       ├── useGreetingForm.ts   # form state
│   │   │       ├── greetingFormSchema.ts  # Effect Schema for the form
│   │   │       ├── *.test.ts(x)         # co-located tests
│   │   │       └── index.ts             # public surface: GreetingPage
│   │   └── features/<feature-name>/     # optional: web code that routes share
│   ├── e2e/                             # the behaviour map: greeting.spec.ts, accessibility.spec.ts
│   ├── etc/                             # generated API reports
│   └── vite.config.ts                   # proxies /trpc to API_ORIGIN (default http://127.0.0.1:3001)
└── api/                                 # @repo/api, Node with native type stripping
    ├── src/
    │   ├── server.ts                    # composition root: the HTTP server on PORT (default 3001)
    │   ├── router.ts                    # appRouter and the AppRouter type
    │   ├── trpc.ts                      # initTRPC: router, procedure, createCallerFactory
    │   └── features/
    │       └── greeting/
    │           ├── index.ts             # public surface: greetingRouter
    │           ├── procedures.ts        # validates input, delegates to application
    │           ├── application.ts       # use cases: greet
    │           ├── domain.ts            # pure types and rules: Greeting, formatGreeting
    │           ├── integrations.ts      # storage and every effect (the greeting has none)
    │           └── *.test.ts
    ├── etc/
    └── package.json                     # exports only { ".": { "types": "./src/router.ts" } }
packages/ui/                             # @repo/ui, react as its only peer
├── src/
│   ├── Button.tsx
│   ├── TextField.tsx
│   ├── styles.css                       # imported once in main.tsx as '@repo/ui/styles.css'
│   └── index.ts
└── etc/ui.api.md
showcase/<id>/                           # a Todo trial result: the same shape, scope @<id>
├── architecture.mmd                     # generated by pnpm arch:diagram
├── web/                                 # @<id>/web: package.json, index.html, vite.config.ts, src/, e2e/, etc/
└── api/                                 # @<id>/api: package.json, src/, etc/
```

## Roles

[`.fallowrc.jsonc`](../../.fallowrc.jsonc) is the one rules file. Each role is
a Fallow zone, and its patterns match every result through the brace glob
`{apps,showcase/*}`. Fallow fails any value import the table does not allow,
and `coverage.requireAllFiles` fails any source file that sits in no role. A
role may import types (`import type`, `export type … from`) from any other
role ([ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)).
Inline `type` specifiers count too, as in `import { type Greeting }`, when
every specifier carries one. Fallow reads a plain `import { Greeting }` as a
value import even when the file uses `Greeting` only as a type, so write
`import type`.
A slice of a role still imports nothing from a sibling slice. Paths below are
relative to a result root (`apps/` or `showcase/<id>/`).

| Role | Files | May import |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `web-app` | `web/src/main.tsx`, `web/src/App.tsx`, `web/src/index.css` | `web-routes`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `web-api-client` | `web/src/api-client/**` | no other role |
| `web-routes` | `web/src/routes/<route>/**` | `web-features`, `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `web-features` | `web/src/features/<feature>/**` | `web-api-client`, `ui` |
| `ui` | `packages/ui/src/**` | no other role |
| `api-app` | `api/src/server.ts`, `api/src/router.ts` | `api-trpc`, `api-procedures` |
| `api-trpc` | `api/src/trpc.ts` | no other role |
| `api-procedures` | `api/src/features/<name>/{index,procedures}.ts`, `features/<name>/procedures/**` | `api-trpc`, `api-application` |
| `api-application` | `api/src/features/<name>/application.ts`, `features/<name>/application/**` | `api-domain`, `api-integrations` |
| `api-domain` | `api/src/features/<name>/domain.ts`, `features/<name>/domain/**` | no other role |
| `api-integrations` | `api/src/features/<name>/integrations.ts`, `features/<name>/integrations/**` | `api-domain` |

Tests (`*.test.ts(x)`), `web/e2e/**`, `web/index.html`, `web/vite.config.ts`
and `etc/**` sit outside the roles. A file that grows too large becomes a
folder of the same name, such as `features/<name>/application/`, and keeps its
role.

The canonical diagram [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd)
shows every role and every value direction the rules allow. Each result has
its own generated diagram,
[`apps/architecture.mmd`](../../apps/architecture.mmd) for the reference and
`showcase/<id>/architecture.mmd` for a trial, with the role edges its imports
resolve to. An edge is dashed where the contract allows its pair for types
only. A type-only import along a direction that also allows values draws
solid, because Fallow's graph records no import kind; the trial comparison
reads the sources and counts that edge as type-only. Both come from
`pnpm arch:diagram`, with the same node names.

## Result structure

`tooling/architecture/structure.mjs` checks every result alike, the reference
included ([ADR 0033](../decisions/0033-result-diagrams-and-structure-validation.md)):

- Each web package holds a source file in `web-app`, `web-api-client` and
  `web-routes`, and each api package in `api-app`, `api-trpc`,
  `api-procedures`, `api-application` and `api-domain`. A test file holds no
  role.
- A result root holds `web/`, `api/` and `architecture.mmd`. A web package
  holds `package.json`, `index.html`, `vite.config.ts`, `src/`, `public/`,
  `e2e/` and `etc/`. An api package holds `package.json`, `src/` and `etc/`.
  The root configs own every gate, so every tool config, at any depth, lives
  at the repository root. A result holds regular files, so copy a file
  rather than link it.
- A manifest is named `@<scope>/<kind>`. Its other fields, scripts included,
  equal the reference package of its kind, and it lists a subset of that
  package's dependencies with the same ranges. A web package lists its
  own `@<scope>/api` and `@repo/ui` as workspace dependencies; an api package
  lists only external ones.
- A web package holds at least one `e2e/**/*.spec.ts`, the specs Playwright runs.
- Each import stays inside its result or reaches `packages/ui`.
- A result fixes each finding in code, so it holds no suppression directive,
  ESLint inline config in a block comment, `/* global */` comment or coverage
  pragma.

## The api file roles

| File | Holds | Shape in the greeting feature |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `procedures.ts` | The feature's tRPC router. Each procedure validates its input with `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`, with `Schema` from `effect`, and delegates to application. It maps application errors to `TRPCError`. | `greetingRouter = router({ greet: procedure.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(greetInputSchema)).query(({ input }) => greet(input)) })` |
| `application.ts` | The use cases. It calls domain rules and integrations and knows no transport. | `greet(request)` returns `{ message: formatGreeting(request.name) }` |
| `domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. It imports nothing by value: no tRPC, no Effect, no Node. | `Greeting`, `formatGreeting(name)` |
| `integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect: `fetch`, Node IO, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync`, `Effect.runFork`. Application calls it. | The greeting needs none, so the file is absent. |
| `index.ts` | The public surface: the feature's router. | `export { greetingRouter } from './procedures.ts';` |

The router mounts each feature through its `index.ts`, with the extension:

```ts
// apps/api/src/router.ts
import { greetingRouter } from './features/greeting/index.ts';
import { router } from './trpc.ts';

export const appRouter = router({ greeting: greetingRouter });
export type AppRouter = typeof appRouter;
```

Every relative import in the api names its `.ts` extension, because Node runs
the source directly (`node src/server.ts`) and `tsconfig.api.json` resolves
with `NodeNext`. Web code imports without extensions (`./routes/greeting`),
because Vite resolves it.

## The web state model

| State | Owner | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` with `trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryOptions(input)` or `.mutationOptions(options)` | a `use*` hook in the route folder, such as `useGreeting.ts` |
| Form state | React Hook Form: `useForm({ resolver: standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema)), defaultValues })` | `use<Name>Form.ts`, with the schema in `<name>FormSchema.ts` in Effect Schema |
| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |

A component calls its hooks and renders. It holds no state, effect, query,
mutation or form of its own.

Any web role may name an api type with `import type` from `@repo/api`. The api
client is the only web module that wires the tRPC client and imports its
packages, `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query`. Everything else
reaches the api through `useTrpc()` from `../../api-client`:

```ts
// a query, as in apps/web/src/routes/greeting/useGreeting.ts
const trpc = useTrpc();
const query = useQuery(trpc.greeting.greet.queryOptions(name === null ? skipToken : { name }));

// a mutation that refreshes a query on success
const queryClient = useQueryClient();
const mutation = useMutation(
  trpc.<router>.<procedure>.mutationOptions({
    onSuccess: () =>
      queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() }),
  }),
);
```

Route and hook tests render through `TestApiProvider` with one typed handler
per procedure path. They exercise the real hooks and providers, with no mocked
hook. See `apps/web/src/routes/greeting/GreetingPage.test.tsx`:

```tsx
function renderPage(greet: NonNullable<TestApiHandlers['greeting.greet']>) {
  const view = render(
    <TestApiProvider handlers={{ 'greeting.greet': greet }}>
      <GreetingPage />
    </TestApiProvider>,
  );
  return { ...view, user: userEvent.setup() };
}
```

A procedure the test gives no handler fails with
`TestApiProvider has no handler for <path>`.

## The rules (and why)

Each rule fails a check on a seeded violation in a committed test
(`tooling/architecture/boundaries.test.ts`, `scripts/eslint-policy.test.ts`,
`tooling/architecture/typescript.test.ts`). The check's message names the fix.

| Rule | Why | Enforced by | Proved by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routes own page composition. | One place per page keeps navigation readable. | ESLint `policy/pages-in-routes`, Fallow `web-routes` | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |
| Sibling slices stand alone: a route imports no other route, a feature no other feature. | Each slice changes without breaking its siblings. | ESLint `policy/slice-isolation` for every result; Fallow child zones for the `apps/web` routes | `pnpm lint:policy`, `pnpm arch:gate` |

## Architecture checks

`pnpm arch:check` runs in `pnpm verify` and runs three checks over the rules
file:

- `pnpm arch:gate` runs `fallow architecture` and exits 1 on a forbidden import
  or a file in no role. It then runs the structure check above and
  `diagram.mjs --check`, which exits 1 on a missing, stale or extra diagram.
- `pnpm arch:diagram` regenerates
  [`docs/architecture/roles.mmd`](../../docs/architecture/roles.mmd) and every
  result's `architecture.mmd`. Commit the result; CI fails when a committed copy
  differs from a fresh run.
- `pnpm api:check` compares the API reports with the code. `pnpm api:report`
  rewrites them per package: the package entry gives
  `<package>/etc/<name>.api.md` (`apps/api/etc/api.api.md`), and each route,
  feature and api-client `index.ts` gives `<package>/etc/<folder>-<name>.api.md`
  (`apps/web/etc/routes-greeting.api.md`, `apps/api/etc/features-greeting.api.md`,
  `apps/web/etc/api-client.api.md`). Commit the reports with the change.

`pnpm arch:gate` also reports the `contract/<id>` rules in every file an entry
point reaches. `pnpm fallow:audit` runs them over the files a change touches,
with `audit.gate: "all"`, so it fails every finding there, inherited ones
included.

## Showcase results

A showcase result is the output of one Todo trial
([ADR 0034](../decisions/0034-trial-harness-and-evidence.md)). The trial
harness writes it into `showcase/<id>/` of a fresh clone, and its evidence
lands in `docs/trials/<id>.json`.

- Give it the reference's layout, roles, scripts and dependencies, with its
  id as the npm scope (`@todo-01/web`, `@todo-01/api`).
- Depend only on its own api (types only) and `@repo/ui`; a result imports
  nothing from another result.
- Every gate reaches it by the same globs as the reference, with no config
  entry of its own; `tooling/trial/inclusion.test.ts` proves it.
- Coverage holds per result: each result reaches 80 percent on its own
  (`tooling/coverage-by-result.mjs`).
- Besides its own `web/e2e/*.spec.ts`, Playwright runs the fixed acceptance
  spec `tooling/trial/acceptance/todo.spec.ts` against it as `<id>-acceptance`.
- Its structure, public API, dependencies, component boundaries and
  conventions are compared with every other run, failed runs included, in
  `docs/trials/comparison.md`, which `node tooling/trial/compare.mjs`
  generates ([ADR 0035](../decisions/0035-trial-comparison.md)). Keep each
  difference inside a spec freedom that ADR or
  [ADR 0037](../decisions/0037-type-only-edges-and-flagged-re-exports.md)
  lists: a type-only import between roles, and dropping a re-export a gate
  flagged, are among them.

## What this template intentionally omits

The template leaves out a router library, a store, a database and auth. They
are stack choices, not agentic principles. A result keeps its data in memory
inside `integrations.ts`. When you add one of them, record the choice as an ADR
in [`../decisions/`](../decisions) and give it a role in `.fallowrc.jsonc`.

## How to extend

Use the greeting feature as the model at every step. Paths are shown for the
reference result; a trial result uses `showcase/<id>/` in place of `apps/`.

### Add an api feature

1. Create `apps/api/src/features/<name>/` (kebab-case) with `domain.ts`,
   `application.ts`, `procedures.ts` and `index.ts`. Add `integrations.ts` for
   storage or any effect.
2. Write the domain and application tests first, then a procedures test through
   `createCallerFactory(<name>Router)({})`, as in
   `apps/api/src/features/greeting/procedures.test.ts`.
3. Mount the router in `apps/api/src/router.ts`: import
   `./features/<name>/index.ts` and add it to `router({ ... })`.

### Add a procedure

1. Add the input schema in `procedures.ts` and pass it as
   `.input(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))`.
2. End with `.query(...)` for a read and `.mutation(...)` for a write, and
   delegate to one application function.
3. Cover the valid input and the rejected input (`BAD_REQUEST`) in
   `procedures.test.ts`.

### Add a route

1. Create `apps/web/src/routes/<route-name>/` with `<Name>Page.tsx` and an
   `index.ts` that exports the page.
2. Put server state in `use<Name>.ts` through `useTrpc()`, form state in
   `use<Name>Form.ts` and `<name>FormSchema.ts`, and each component in its own
   file built from `@repo/ui` primitives.
3. Test the page and hooks through `TestApiProvider`.
4. Mount the page in `apps/web/src/App.tsx`.
5. Specify the behaviour in `apps/web/e2e/<route-name>.spec.ts`. Playwright
   runs every spec in that folder.

### Add a web feature

Create `apps/web/src/features/<feature-name>/` with an `index.ts` when web code
is reused across routes. It may import the api client and `@repo/ui`; routes
import it through its `index.ts`.

### Finish

1. Run `pnpm api:report` and commit the new or changed `etc/*.api.md`.
2. Run `pnpm arch:diagram` and commit `apps/architecture.mmd` and
   `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` when they change.
3. `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` pass before you call it done.

## Contract rules

The Fallow rule pack
[`tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc`](../../tooling/architecture/contract.rules.jsonc)
reports each finding as `policy-violation` `contract/<id>`, an error. Tests are
outside every rule.

| Rule id | What it keeps |
| --- | --- |
| `contract/domain-pure` | `domain.ts` imports no `@trpc/server`, no `effect` and no Node module. `tsconfig.domain.json` also gives it no Node globals. |
| `contract/application-without-trpc` | `application.ts` imports no `@trpc/server`; procedures map errors to tRPC. |
| `contract/effects-in-integrations` | `fetch`, `self.fetch`, `Effect.runPromise`, `Effect.runSync` and `Effect.runFork` run only in `integrations.ts` or the api `server.ts` and `router.ts`. |
| `contract/io-effects-in-integrations` | Network, storage, process and shell work runs only there too. |
| `contract/node-io-in-integrations` | Node IO modules (`fs`, `http`, `net`, `child_process`) are imported only there too. |
| `contract/trpc-client-in-api-client` | `@trpc/client` and `@trpc/tanstack-react-query` are imported only in `web/src/api-client/`. |
| `contract/trpc-server-off-the-web` | Web and ui code imports `@trpc/server` only in `web/src/api-client/`. |
| `contract/ui-without-logic` | `packages/ui` imports no query, form, schema or tRPC library. |

## State ownership

| State | Owner | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Server state | TanStack Query through `useTrpc()` from the api client, with `queryOptions` or `mutationOptions` | `use<Name>.ts` in the route folder (`useGreeting.ts`) |
| Form state | React Hook Form with `standardSchemaResolver(Schema.toStandardSchemaV1(schema))` and `defaultValues` | `use<Name>Form.ts` (`useGreetingForm.ts`) |
| Form schema | Effect Schema | `<name>FormSchema.ts` (`greetingFormSchema.ts`) |
| Local UI state | `useState` or `useReducer` | a `use*` hook |

After a mutation, refresh the queries it changes in `onSuccess` with
`queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: trpc.<router>.<procedure>.queryKey() })`.

| File | Holds |
| --- | --- |
| `features/<name>/procedures.ts` | The feature router. Validates each input with `Schema.toStandardSchemaV1` and delegates to application. |
| `features/<name>/application.ts` | Use cases. Calls domain and integrations; knows no transport. |
| `features/<name>/domain.ts` | Pure types and rules. |
| `features/<name>/integrations.ts` | Storage, including in-memory storage, and every effect. |
| `features/<name>/index.ts` | The public surface: the feature router. |

greeting reference.

## Judgment calls

- **Full words in identifiers.** Write `name` and `request`. The name is the
  cheapest documentation an agent has. Established acronyms such as E2E, CI,
  ADR, UI, IO, and URL are fine.
- **Hooks wire state, components render, pure functions hold logic.** See
  [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md).
- **Build with `@repo/ui` primitives.** Use `Button` and `TextField` for
  controls, and add a primitive to `packages/ui` when a result needs a new one.
- **Validate data at an IO boundary.** Parse network, storage, and environment
  data before trusting its type, as `server.ts` decodes `PORT` with Effect
  Schema. A type assertion is a claim, and validation is proof.
- **Fail loudly at boundaries.** `main.tsx` throws when `#root` is missing.

# Definition of Done

A change is **done** when every box below is true. This is not aspirational —
the quality gates mechanically enforce most of it, so "done" and "passes the
gates" are the same statement. A task is not done until the changed behaviour is
verified by deterministic evidence: tests, build output, typecheck and lint
results, screenshots or video for user-visible behaviour, or another concrete
artifact that stands without anyone's judgment. An agent reports a task
complete once `pnpm verify` and `pnpm e2e` are green.

## The checklist

- [ ] **Behaviour is specified.** New or changed behaviour is covered by a
      spec in the result's `web/e2e/` folder (the behaviour map), such as
      `apps/web/e2e/greeting.spec.ts`. The product's contract is explicit.
- [ ] **Logic is unit-tested.** Domain, application and procedures have `api`
      Jest tests; hooks and pages have `web` Jest tests that render through
      `TestApiProvider`. Coverage stays at/above the threshold in
      `jest.config.ts` (80%).
- [ ] **Types check.** `pnpm typecheck` passes its four programs,
      `tsconfig.json` (web and ui), `tsconfig.node.json` (configs and e2e),
      `tsconfig.api.json` (api) and `tsconfig.domain.json` (api domain, no
      Node), with no `any` and no weakened config.
- [ ] **Lint + format clean.** `pnpm check` (Biome), `pnpm lint:policy`
      (ESLint), and `pnpm react-doctor` pass; every disabled rule carries a
      written reason.
- [ ] **Code intelligence clean.** `pnpm fallow:audit` reports no dead code,
      circular dependency, complexity, architecture or `contract/<id>` finding
      in any file the change touches.
- [ ] **Architecture checks pass.** `pnpm arch:check` passes: every file sits
      in a role, no forbidden import, every result passes the structure check,
      `docs/architecture/roles.mmd` and each result's `architecture.mmd` match
      `pnpm arch:diagram`, and every package's `etc/*.api.md` matches the code
      (`pnpm api:report` after an intended export change).
- [ ] **Build succeeds.** `pnpm build` produces a clean production bundle.
- [ ] **Accessible.** No axe violations (jest-axe in unit tests, `@axe-core/playwright`
      in the E2E run); interactive elements are reachable and labelled.
- [ ] **Within budget.** `pnpm size` passes (the bundle stays under the
      `.size-limit.json` budget).
- [ ] **PR proof is ready.** The pull request body follows
      [`PR_QUALITY.md`](PR_QUALITY.md) and the
      [pull request template](../../.github/pull_request_template.md), with exact
      local commands, visual proof or `Not applicable` with a reason, CI status,
      risk, rollback, and no private details.
- [ ] **Patterns followed.** The change matches
      [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md) and [`CONVENTIONS.md`](CONVENTIONS.md);
      new files were created from [`../templates/`](../templates).
- [ ] **Decisions recorded.** Any new architectural choice is captured as an ADR
      in [`../decisions/`](../decisions). `pnpm check:adr` fails a change that
      adds a dependency unless an ADR added in the same change names it.
- [ ] **Commit is conventional.** Message follows Conventional Commits.

## The one-command proof

```bash
pnpm verify   # typecheck → biome → eslint → fallow → architecture → unit tests → build → size
pnpm e2e      # every result's behaviour map + axe accessibility scan
```

If both are green and the checklist holds, the work is done. If either is red,
it is not — regardless of how finished the code looks.

## PR contract checks

The `PR quality` workflow runs
[`scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs`](../../scripts/validate-pr-body.mjs) on every
pull request event, including edits to the body. It fails the PR with a message
that names the fix unless:

- the body keeps the four [template](../../.github/pull_request_template.md)
  sections in order, each with real content: `Why does this feature exist?`,
  `What changed?`, `Behavioural Proof (with video and screenshots)`, and
  `Verification Summary`;
- the proof section embeds a screenshot inline with `![alt](url)`, or says
  `Not applicable` followed by the technical reason on the same line or the
  next one;
- every inline image is an absolute `https://` URL, and a GitHub blob URL ends
  in `?raw=1`, so the image renders;
- the proof section embeds its images instead of linking to them;
- the title is Conventional Commits, `type(scope): summary`, with no agent or
  tool prefix;
- the head branch is `<type>/<short-kebab-summary>`;
- the Verification Summary has exactly one `- Head commit:` line naming one SHA
  (full or short) of the PR head, so a push that moves the head fails until the
  body is re-checked against it
  ([ADR 0029](../decisions/0029-pr-body-names-its-head-commit.md)).

## Proof judgment

These calls need a reviewer:

- Screenshots and video come from the branch under review and show the changed
  behaviour itself. Flows with motion or timing include video when practical.
- E2E tests map to the user-visible behaviour the PR changes.
- Every bug fix ships, in the same change, with the test that would have caught
  it. The test fails on the unfixed code and asserts the user-visible symptom.
- Missing visual proof or E2E coverage comes with a technical reason and the
  replacement verification method.
- Proof files live under `docs/proof/<short-scope>/` on the PR branch, unless
  the PR states a technical reason for another committed location. See
  [`.claude/skills/pr-inline-screenshot-proof/SKILL.md`](../../.claude/skills/pr-inline-screenshot-proof/SKILL.md).
- Each evidence link opens the rendered artifact once the branch is pushed.

## Verification

- Format, lint, typecheck, unit, integration, and E2E checks relevant to the
  changed files run after the final code change.
- The PR lists each command and its pass or fail result.
- The PR separates existing unrelated failures from failures it introduces.
- Each skipped check names its reason, risk, and follow-up owner.
# Glossary — the project's ubiquitous language

Use these terms **exactly**, in identifiers, tests, commits, and prose. Shared
language is how an agent's output reads as if the team wrote it. When a new
domain term appears, add it here in the same change.

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Result** | A pair of workspace packages, `<root>/web` and `<root>/api`, that together make one app. The reference result is `apps/`; each generated trial result is `showcase/<id>/`. `tooling/results.mjs` lists them. |
| **Role** | One row of the role table in `ARCHITECTURE.md`: a set of files (a Fallow zone) and the roles it may import, such as `web-routes` or `api-domain`. Every source file has exactly one role. |
| **Slice** | One folder under a package's `src/routes/` or `src/features/`, such as `routes/greeting` or `api/src/features/greeting`. A slice imports no sibling slice and exposes itself through `index.ts`. |
| **Route** | A web slice under `web/src/routes/<route-name>/` that owns one page (`<Name>Page.tsx`) and its hooks and components. |
| **Feature** | In the web, a shared slice under `web/src/features/<feature-name>/` that routes compose. In the api, a slice under `api/src/features/<name>/` with `procedures.ts`, `application.ts`, `domain.ts` and `integrations.ts`. |
| **Procedure** | One tRPC endpoint, such as `greeting.greet`, declared in a feature's `procedures.ts`. Its path names it in `TestApiProvider` handlers. |
| **Contract** | The architecture rules every result follows, and the checks that enforce them: the Fallow role zones and `contract/<id>` rule pack, the ESLint policy rules, and the TypeScript programs. Listed in `ARCHITECTURE.md`. |
